#1934. Sources: Crystal Palace 'concerns' over Thomas Frank emerge amid new delay

Senior Correspondent AUTHORITY Senior football correspondent and podcast host with specialist knowledge across the Premier League and SPFL. FOCUS Transfer news, breaking stories, and behind-the-scenes insight across Arsenal, Liverpool, Celtic, and Manchester United. THE INSIGHT Callum utilises a network of club and industry contacts across the Premier League and SPFL to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides the depth behind the headlines — from breaking transfer news to behind-the-scenes developments — ensuring fans get the full story as it happens.

Crystal Palace are still working on a deal to appoint Thomas Frank as their new manager, sources have told Football Insider.

The Eagles had hoped to land a quick appointment following Pierre Sage's dismissal earlier this week, and have been locked in talks with the former Brentford boss as a result.

A full agreement has not yet been reached, despite suggestions that the manager has been keen to take over at Selhurst Park and that talks had been positive.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, the delays surrounding Frank's appointment are due to attempts to land his backroom staff.

Crystal Palace fans will remember the summer of 2021, when Nuno Espirito Santo looked set to take over, before the club pulled the plug due to his overinflated backroom team.

This situation is believed to be different, with optimism on both sides that a deal will be agreed before too long, but concerns are starting to creep in at Selhurst Park.

Football Insider exclusively revealed on 12 November that Crystal Palace have faced delays in Frank's appointment with work ongoing to land the manager's backroom staff.

The Eagles are keen to provide Frank with their backing by bringing in a number of his most trusted allies, as they did with Sage following his arrival from Lens.

However, that has led to delays in the appointment and despite their confidence and having wanted to do a deal quickly, the Eagles remain locked in negotiations.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "What I've been told with regard to Frank is that there are also discussions about the backroom staff who would come in with him.

"There was, I think, three or four staff who came with him to Tottenham from Brentford. They all left with him when he left Tottenham, and he would be looking for them to come in at Palace.

"Palace fans will remember a couple of years ago, before Patrick Vieira came to the club, Palace were close to bringing in Nuno Espirito Santo.

"Eventually, they pulled the plug on that because of difficulties with his backroom staff. They didn't want to pay for what they viewed as sort of an overinflated team.

"I don't think that will be the situation with Frank. I don't think it'll there'll be any sort of major concerns on that. It's just something that maybe Palace have to get over the line.

"Frank will want to bring these people with him and hopefully they'll help him be a success at Palace."

Despite optimism that Frank will still be the next Crystal Palace manager, a number of potential alternatives have already been assessed amid the ongoing delays.

The likes of Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards have been linked with the position, alongside a number of lesser-known names from across European football.

Meanwhile, former Man United coach Mick Brown told Football Insider that Crystal Palace would be making a mistake if they did not appoint Sean Dyche as their next manager.

Defensive issues have been the main concern for Crystal Palace this season, and the former Everton boss has been backed as the man to ease those worries.

Meanwhile, Dyche would bring a clear and recognisable style of play, while questions have been asked about Frank's tactical setup after his struggles as Tottenham manager.

#1933. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#1932. Sources: Coventry's chances of selling Jack Rudoni in January revealed amid Newcastle and Leeds interest

Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. Newcastle United and Leeds United are among a number of clubs tracking Coventry City midfielder Jack Rudoni, sources have told Football Insider.

The 25-year-old will have just one year remaining on his contract at the CBS Arena next summer, with an agreement over a new deal yet to be found.

The London-born talent has adapted well to the Premier League, netting three goals in his last five league games as Frank Lampard's side have stabilised after a difficult start.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Rudoni's future will not be decided in the January transfer window.

A move next summer is more likely, although Coventry will continue to hold out hope of striking an agreement over a new deal for the midfielder.

Their chances will lie with their Premier League status, with relegation likely ending any hopes of keeping hold of the Englishman.

Football Insider revealed this week that Coventry are confident of keeping Rudoni at the club if they stay up, but the likes of Newcastle will be ready to pounce if they do not.

The 25-year-old is of particular interest to the Magpies, with space set to be opening up in Matthias Jaissle's midfield next summer.

Joe Willock's contract is due to expire, and Joelinton could join him in leaving the club with his own deal having entered its final two years.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "If they don’t stay up and they go down there’ll be a number of clubs, not just Newcastle, who would be interested in Rudoni.

"There’s been talk of Leeds interested and there’s interest from abroad as well in Rudoni as well. But look, Coventry aren't even contemplating losing such a key player like Rudoni in January.

"He will be key for Frank Lampard's side as they look to try and secure their Premier League survival as well. The interest is not surprising and obviously his contract, he has only got about 18 months left on his current deal as well.

"That’s why clubs will be sitting up and taking notice of Jack Rudoni as well. But Coventry won’t be entertaining any offers for him for sure."

Despite Coventry's struggles in the Premier League this season, Rudoni has enjoyed a rapid adaptation.

Remarkably, the midfielder is averaging 2.08 chances created, 1.95 successful crosses and 1.10 successful dribbles per game.

He also wins 4.88 duels per game and ranks in the 80th percentile for defensive contributions among Premier League midfielders, making 8.30 per game.

While it is unclear if Coventry will survive the drop this season, Rudoni looks certain to remain in the Premier League.

#1931. Tom Brady QUITS Birmingham City just three years after investing in the club - with Blues top of the Championship

Published: 16:22 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 21:57 EST, 9 November 2026

Tom Brady has sensationally quit Birmingham City just three years after becoming involved with the Championship club.

The Blues said in a statement, released Monday night: 'Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

'It was amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.'

The NFL icon joined Birmingham City as a minority investor as part of a takeover spearheaded by billionaire Tom Wagner's Knighthead Capital in the summer of 2023.

Brady's presence in the English football pyramid was heralded with a five-part documentary on the new ownership's plan to revamp the Midlands club, titled: 'Built in Birmingham: Brady and the Blues'.

Within the five-part Amazon series, Brady notably lambasted Wayne Rooney for his work ethic after installing him briefly in the dugout after despatching previous head coach John Eustace.

Tom Brady (right) has quit Birmingham City just three years after his investment in the club

The NFL legend became a minority owner three years ago but has now called it quits

The fly-on-the-wall documentary showed Brady visiting the Birmingham training ground to observe Rooney's team meeting and training session. While driving away, he tells his business manager Ben Rawitz: 'I'm a little worried about our head coach's work ethic.'

Rawitz replies: 'Comes across as lackadaisical.' Rooney was sacked after 83 days in charge.

The documentary later saw Brady admit his error in replacing Eustace with the former England international and reveal that he was warned against making 'sweeping changes' so early in his time with the club.

'I had good advice, "Don’t go in there and make sweeping changes. You guys have time",' said Brady. 'But we made sweeping changes that put us in decline. That was our doing.'

Under the aegis of Brady and Knighthead Capital, Birmingham City have launched what the group see as a 20-year megaproject, with £3billion earmarked for investment in a 'Sports Quarter' in the city.

The 48-acre site in the east of the city is set to feature a new 60,000-seater stadium and training ground above a network of underground transport tunnels.

But since the plan was announced, there have been some wrinkles with the timeline – pushing the stadium's completion deadline from 2029 to 2031.

Daily Mail Sport understands that London-based architects Heatherwick Studio – in conjunction with Kansas City-based Manica – are set to work on a design with a 'chimney theme' in a nod to the city's industrial heritage.

He infamously hired Wayne Rooney as manager, before the former England captain was sacked 83 days later

Peaky Blinders creator and famous Bluenose Steven Knight is believed to be working with the team to ensure it is 'one of the most-talked about stadium designs ever'.

Last season, Brady had promised promotion to the Premier League. The club are top of the Championship going into the last international break of the year, though he has departed before they can reach the top flight again.

Brady's involvement had been lauded by Wagner, and his departure was met with a mixed reaction by fans on social media.

One wrote on X: 'Didn't contribute anything after the first season, good riddance.'

Another wrote: 'What did he even do? Even his fitness guy didn't contribute anything, we had more injuries than ever.

'PR stunt, better off without him being involved. Embarrassed us on the Amazon doc too.'

A third, though, posted: 'Some of these clueless comments. He's a brand name and he made us globally talked about, globally looked at, globally listened to.

#1930. MN: Allegri expressed ‘annoyance’ over Milan’s €8m deal for Cisse – the reasons

Alphadjo Cisse is the man of the moment for AC Milan, and yet there were some within the club at the time who opposed his arrival.

Cisse is currently the top scorer in the team with eight goals to his name, earning him a senior Italian national team call-up from Roberto Mancini. All this for a player who missed the first half of 2026 due to injury and has only just turned 20.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is now talk of Premier League clubs expressing their interest in signing him, but in the meantime Milan have a counter-move ready: the extension of his contract with a pay rise as a reward.

MilanNews reveal the back story regarding his arrival. In January, Cisse seemed destined to join PSV Eindhoven, but a phone call from Milan changed everything. When the Rossoneri entered the race, the forward put PSV on hold and made it clear where he wanted to go.

Milan then convinced Verona with a bid of €8m and persuaded Cisse with a development plan, including that he could remain on loan in Serie B with Catanzaro. Geoffrey Moncada identified him and Giorgio Furlani was key in the negotiations with his agency CAA Base, too.

However, not everyone at Milan was in favour. The report claims that Massimiliano Allegri did not like the idea of allocating part of the budget on a young player while his side were in a title fight. Niclas Füllkrug was the only first-team reinforcement, arriving on loan from West Ham.

Allegri did not fail to express his ‘annoyance and negativity’ regarding the Cisse operation, which was later finalised by Furlani. In the end, the head coach, CEO and the chief scout (Moncada) would all be dismissed after the final game of the season.

#1928. Ex-Hungary captain hits out at ‘sobbing’ Andoni Iraola after Dominik Szoboszlai injury comments

A former captain of the Hungary national team has criticised Andoni Iraola for his treatment of Dominik Szoboszlai amid an injury concern to the Liverpool midfielder.

The 26-year-old sprained his knee in the first half of the 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace last weekend but continued playing until the 69th minute until he was replaced by Trey Nyoni.

The Reds’ head coach made a thinly-veiled plea afterwards for our number 8 to not feature for his country during this international window, with the Hungarian FA subsequently stating that they’ll defer any decision on his involvement against Georgia and Northern Ireland for as long as possible.

In quotes published by the print edition of Blikk (via Sport Witness), ex-Hungary goalkeeper Janos Csank blasted Iraola for not substituting Szoboszlai at half-time in the win over Palace.

The 80-year-old raged: “I was really annoyed. Szoboszlai went down on the pitch in the first half, and at half-time I was certain he wouldn’t come back on for the second half. Then I saw him standing there on the pitch, with black tape on his leg, his knee.

“Then the manager starts sobbing that he is injured. He should have been substituted straight away; they were leading 1-0. Half-time comes and then he sends him back on injured with his knee bandaged?! I’m losing my mind! I just don’t get it.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

As head coach of Liverpool, the club to whom Szoboszlai is contracted, Iraola is well within his rights to utilise the player as he sees fit, and any decision to send him back out for the second half would surely have been taken in consultation with the medical staff.

We admit that, if that had happened on international duty, we’d be pleading for Marco Rossi to exercise caution and substitute the 26-year-old immediately. Every stakeholder will inevitably shout the loudest in favour of their best interests.

In a similar vein, Reds supporters will hope that the midfielder isn’t deemed fit enough to play for his country in the coming week and instead recover for the Manchester United game the following Sunday, whereas he’ll be striving to prove his fitness in time to face Georgia on Saturday.

Szoboszlai has almost always been available during his three-and-a-bit years as a Liverpool player, although he’s had an injury-hit few weeks of late, having only recently overcome a thigh problem which resurfaced during the win at Brentford last month.

Everyone of a Reds persuasion will face a nervous wait over the next week or so to see whether Iraola will have any fresh injury worries once our season resumes in 10 days’ time. Fingers crossed that everyone on international duty gets back to Merseyside unscathed.

The Scottish businessman feels that a loan move with Enzo Maresca's side contributing a significant chunk of his wages could be the best way forward.

#1926. “It’s a special place” – Liverpool confirm Anfield return for James Milner

Liverpool FC have confirmed on Thursday that James Milner will return to Anfield in 2027.

Signed on a free transfer from Manchester City in 2015, the former Reds midfielder spent eight years on Merseyside and became vice-captain under Jurgen Klopp, winning the Premier League and Champions League among other trophies in his time with the club.

The 40-year-old closed out his playing career at Brighton, announcing his retirement this summer after setting the record for the most Premier League seasons appeared in (24 consecutively from 2002/03 to 2025/26).

As announced via liverpoolfc.com on Thursday lunchtime, Milner is the first player to be confirmed for the next Liverpool Legends match, which takes place against Inter Milan at Anfield on Saturday 27 March 2027, with proceeds going towards the LFC Foundation.

The Reds’ former vice-captain said of his participation in the fixture: “I’m thrilled to have the chance to pull on the red shirt again and step back out at Anfield. It’s a special place, and playing there in front of the supporters is a feeling like no other.

“What makes the legends match so special is that it’s about more than football. It’s a chance to give something back to the fans while supporting the work of the LFC Foundation. I’m delighted to be the first to sign up and can’t wait to be part of it.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The news of Milner’s participation in the 2027 Legends match is sure to go down a treat with Liverpool fans who adored him for his humility and commitment to the cause in his eight years as a Red, along with his excellence as a player.

The Yorkshire native was renowned for setting exceptionally high standards within the playing group and enjoyed near-annual domination of the infamous pre-season lactate test, and he commands universal respect among his peers and the wider football community.

The Reds were lucky enough to be the club that he represented more times than any other, with 322 of his 903 senior appearances coming for the Merseysiders (Transfermarkt).

He’ll now get to line out in a Liverpool shirt at Anfield once more, and while it mightn’t be in a competitive fixture, the reception won’t be any less rapturous for a player whose supreme attitude characterised a glorious era for LFC.

As ever, it promises to be a wonderful occasion in which thousands of pounds will be raised for a most worthy cause, and Kopites will get to enjoy seeing many former greats of the club return for one afternoon.

#1923. Rumoured Liverpool transfer target has been told to find a new club; he left Van Dijk bemused

One player who’s recently been linked with a move to Liverpool has reportedly been told that he’s free to leave his current club.

Two years on from being first linked with Malo Gusto, the Reds are understood to have maintained their interest in the Chelsea full-back and even made enquiries about him during the summer (TEAMtalk).

The same outlet reported that the Blues are seemingly holding out for a world-record fee for a right-back, which is currently held by Achraf Hakimi when he joined Paris Saint-Germain for €68m (then £60m) in June 2021.

According to Si Phillips Talks Chelsea, Xabi Alonso has told the French defender that ‘it is time he finds a new club’, with the ex-Liverpool midfielder preferring to put his trust in Marco Palestra and Josh Acheampong for the long-term.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The 23-year-old made a name for himself at Anfield just a couple of weeks ago, but not for the most positive of reasons.

The Chelsea right-back melodramatically threw himself to the ground after mild contact from Virgil van Dijk, who simply looked bemused by the Frenchman’s reaction, and he also petulantly waved his boot at the assistant referee in a futile attempt to get Bradley Barcola yellow-carded.

It’d definitely make a lot more sense than paying upwards of £60m for the Stamford Bridge defender, especially if Jeremie Frimpong and/or Conor Bradley were to regain form and fitness in the second half of this season.

#1922. USMNT fans in meltdown as head coach Mauricio Pochettino emerges as frontrunner for Manchester United job

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 21:47 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 23:51 EST, 9 November 2026

US soccer fans were sent into a frenzy on Monday by the news that Mauricio Pochettino is in pole position to join Manchester United.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Michael Carrick is facing the sack with United bosses leaning towards hiring a new coach during the international break.

Pochettino has emerged as a frontrunner for the role, despite signing a new contract following the World Cup, when he led the USMNT to the last 16.

The Argentine committed his future to the end of the next World Cup in 2030 but his contract includes a £7 million ($9.4 million) release clause. And news of Manchester United's interest left many USMNT fans fearing the worst.

'[That] was fun while it lasted!' one said. 'Wow - just when you thought things had settled a bit with the USMNT!' added a second, while a third said: 'Noooo they can’t have our coach!'

Many other supporters on social media refused to believe that Pochettino could leave but his future has been under the microscope ever since he took over in September 2024.

Mauricio Pochettino is in pole position to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Carrick is facing the sack with United leaning towards hiring a new coach in the coming weeks

The 54-year-old Pochettino has made no secret of his desire to return to the Premier League

The 54-year-old has made no secret of his desire to return to the Premier League, while it emerged ahead of the World Cup that he had held discussions with AC Milan.

Pochettino's team sparkled en route to the last 16, only to crash out against Belgium after President Trump's intervention over the red card shown to striker Folarin Balogun.

His initial contract expired after the tournament but after weeks of uncertainty, the former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton coach signed a four-year extension.

He is slated to take charge of a Nations League double-header against Haiti during this international break, with a press conference set for Friday.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

#1921. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. #1919. Steven Gerrard explains his theory on why Alexis Mac Allister has been so resurgent this season

Steven Gerrard has offered a theory as to why Alexis Mac Allister has looked so resurgent this season compared to last.

The midfielder was one of the Reds’ most disappinting players of a dreadful 2025/26 campaign, especially having been such a key component in the preceding Premier League title triumph, but he’s been playing near to his best since Andoni Iraola took charge in the summer.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily (via Liverpool Echo), our former captain claimed that the 27-year-old subconsciously let his performance levels drop last season as he was privately consumed by trying to retain the World Cup with Argentina.

Gerrard said of Mac Allister: “I’ve loved him this season. I think last year, like a lot of the Argentinian players, they had a bit of a distraction with the World Cup coming up.

“It’s the way they are. The World Cup takes over everything in their lives, and I lived that with Emiliano Martínez when I was at Aston Villa. I just think it becomes a priority.

“I think it becomes a bit of a distraction. It becomes the most important thing in their lives, to be ready and not injured and make sure that the national team is the priority.

“I think with a lot of the Argentina players, I’m sure a lot of managers, if they watch this, will say: ‘Yeah, I’ve experienced that.’”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It’s an interesting theory that Gerrard has put forward to explain why Mac Allister’s performances from last season to this have been so chalk and cheese.

Many footballers consider the World Cup as the pinnacle of their careers, and the Liverpool midfielder represents a nation where the sport is nothing short of an obsession.

Only the 27-year-old could truthfully answer whether or not he let his levels dip in 2025/26 because he was prioritising the global tournament in North America, but from a Reds perspective we’d hope that isn’t the case.

As a player employed by LFC, Mac Allister has a duty to give full commitment to representing the club. As disappointing as his performances were last season, though, we wouldn’t go as far as accusing him of not giving less than 100%, which’d be a serious indictment of an elite footballer.

Thankfully, the Argentine has looked much more like his usual self since August, to the point where Troy Deeney suggested that he would even inspire Liverpool to nudge their way into the Premier League title race if he maintains or improves further upon his current standards.

The 27-year-old has been vocal about his contract situation at Anfield, but if he keeps playing the way that he has been, securing a new deal for him should become a matter of priority for sporting director Richard Hughes.

#1917. James Pearce claim seems to pour cold water over Liverpool links with Finn Jeltsch

Liverpool, it’s fair to say, have a pretty active recruiting department.

A necessarily active recruiting department, it should be emphasised, given the squad-building challenges Andoni Iraola has already faced early on in his tenure as head coach.

The Merseysiders navigated a potential centre-back crisis expertly in the summer with the arrival of loan signing Ronald Araujo from Barcelona. But questions remain as to the long-term viability of the centre-back department post the summer 2027 transfer window.

A recent report from Christian Falk with CF Bayern Insider asserted that Liverpool, among Europe’s elite, have scouted VfB Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch.

“It is TRUE: Liverpool have scouted VfB Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch. All the top clubs, including Bayern Munich, are scouting him,” the head of football at Bild said.

“He was in the squad for Klopp first as a backup for the right-back. Then one of the central defenders became injured, and now he’s also the backup at centre-back. This shows he can play many positions, and everyone can see the 20-year-old’s potential.

“Such players really are a present to everyone. Jeltsch is young, talented and can play many positions, and he’s not so expensive! Bayern Munich has an eye on him.”

If that name seems vaguely familiar, it might be because Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich are already big fans of the footballer and are keeping a very close eye on matters close to home.

Liverpool’s interest is understandable. Come the summer transfer window, they could be two centre-halves down should Joe Gomez and Virgil van Dijk call time on their Anfield careers once their contracts run out. Ronald Araujo, though enjoying an impeccable campaign with the Reds, may not become a permanent addition to the squad, despite Liverpool possessing a buy option. Much here may depend on what Barcelona’s stance on the Uruguayan international looks like in May.

That’s three centre-backs Liverpool could be short come the opening of the summer transfer window, so it’s very plausible that Julian Ward and Co. will be keeping a close eye on the centre-back market between now and the end of the 2026/27 season.

As James Pearce rightly notes on X (formerly Twitter), of course, Liverpool do have several high-potential, highly exciting young centre-backs in their stable.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, by all accounts, is impressing on loan at Levante after an eye-catching pre-season; Giovanni Leoni remains an appetising option, and then there’s hope for young Mor Talla Ndiaye also.

Centre-back not a priority for Liverpool so highly unlikely they will invest heavily in that area either in Jan or next summer. Jacquet has made a huge impact and big hopes for fellow young CBs Leoni, Ndukwe and Ndiaye.

— James Pearce (@JamesPearceLFC) November 13, 2026

But these are three very young, very inexperienced centre-backs you’d be pairing with the also youthful, but extremely impressive, Jeremy Jacquet for the foreseeable future. The Frenchman will, however, have a season of Premier League football under his belt – but is that enough to help guide the next generation of Liverpool centre-backs?

Unless you’re planning to extend Van Dijk’s contract or activate Araujo’s buy option, Liverpool are looking incredibly short on options with experience and genuine leadership credentials at L4.

That might be worth considering if the plan isn’t to invest in Finn Jeltsch this summer.

Harvey Elliott is reportedly set to be sent packing back home to Liverpool in January.

After some concerns were expressed over the former Fulham academy graduate having arrived overweight in the Spanish top-flight, it seems the 23-year-old has been unable to make any headway at Mestalla.

Not a lot of time for the footballer to buck up his ideas and earn himself a place in the hearts of the Valencia fans and, importantly, the decision-makers at the outfit.

It’s not looking great for Harvey Elliott, it has to be said.

After basically being iced out of the Liverpool squad by former Reds head coach Andoni Iraola, the playmaker was shipped off to Unai Emery’s Aston Villa and only picked up 284 minutes of action.

Mind, there seemed to be a weird kind of power play going on between Liverpool and the Villans, with the Reds unwilling to pay a significant amount of cash to cut the loan short and Emery’s side being apparently fine with letting a young player rot on the bench to make a point.

Point made. And now Elliott’s future is paying for it.

We do want to state, unequivocally, that we believe in Harvey Elliott and his potential. It wasn’t a million years ago when we were watching him thriving as part of Jurgen Klopp’s deep squad in the German’s final season in charge in 2023/24. But that season is becoming increasingly distant, and it’s becoming increasingly difficult to imagine Elliott ever playing a significant role for Liverpool again in future.

We hope he can turn things around in Valencia. Because if our No.19 comes back to L4 in January, it’s not an eventuality that will suit the player or the club at this stage.

#1913. Michael Carrick facing the sack at Man United: Mauricio Pochettino the frontrunner to replace beleaguered boss - but chiefs face splashing out £7MILLION for former Spurs and Chelsea coach

Published: 18:04 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 02:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Michael Carrick is facing the sack with Manchester United bosses leaning towards installing a new head coach during the international break.

Carrick’s position has become increasingly precarious after United dropped into the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

It left the 45-year-old with just one win from 10 Premier League games this season – United’s worst start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a new frontrunner to replace Carrick. The Argentine is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

In the three games since then, Carrick’s side lost at Chelsea, staged a remarkable comeback to beat Roma in the Champions League in midweek and then fought back again to draw with Villa.

Michael Carrick is likely to be sacked from his role as Manchester United manager during the international break

It is understood that United officials have not made a final decision, though there is expectation that there will be a new boss in place after the international break

Although it’s understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick’s future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

But this season has unravelled alarmingly for United with his three wins in 15 games in all competitions coming at home to newly-promoted Ipswich in the Premier League as well as Sabah of Azerbaijan and Roma in the Champions League.

Asked after Sunday’s chaotic draw with Villa if he would consider quitting, a defiant Carrick said: ‘That's not going to happen.

‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation and where we are. But we can do something about it. I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games.’

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Ferguson retired 13-and-a-half years ago.

Pochettino was strongly linked with the job when Erik ten Hag was appointed in 2022 and again when the Dutchman was sacked two years later.

The 54-year-old has extensive Premier League experience at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton and was also in charge at Paris Saint-Germain.

Current US boss - and former Tottenham and Chelsea manager - Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the frontrunner to replace Carrick

Howe was previously seen as the favourite but it’s understood there has been no contact between United and the former Newcastle boss.

It would cost United around £3million in compensation to appoint the 48-year-old under the terms of his departure from St James’s Park in July.

Nagelsmann is available after leaving his role as head coach of the German national team in the summer when they were eliminated from the World Cup following a penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay in the round of 32.

#1909. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

“It is another opportunity for fitness. Coming into games against teams of good quality, it is important we get good fitness. It is a chance to build momentum for the season ahead. We are taking steps in the right direction. Of course, we want more from the performance and the results, but we take learnings and move on.

“All of us, together, we share a common goal. We have confidence to build on. We will take every game as it comes. The atmosphere was amazing. I did not realise Ireland has so many Arsenal fans. We are so grateful for everyone who came to support us today. We wanted to give them a good result and performance. Hopefully next time we can.”

“We always want to win and in the end we could not today. In some ways they deserved it and we could have done better. We did have some good moments though. We had an amazing season last season. I believe in this team and there are still players to come back from the World Cup. I am confident but we can always do better.”

Isco should put Betis 4-1 up but tries to be too cute and clever. Former Arsenal man Bellerin delivers a cross from the right side of the box and picks out a free Isco in the six-yard box. Salmon is deceived by a dummy by Riquelme and then brings the Betis man down, earning him a yellow card.

Copley is helped off by the two Arsenal medics, shaking his head and not putting any weight on his left leg, and is replaced by Julienne.

You have to hope that the knee injury to Louie Copley is not serious but judging by the way he went down largely unchallenged, his reaction and the way he was being helped down the tunnel it didn’t look too good. A tough moment for the youngster who had only been on the pitch nine minutes.

Play is halted as Copley has been down for a little while clutching at his left knee. He got his studs stuck in the ground and went down in some pain. The medics come on to check that left knee. He only came on at half-time but his night is over not even 10 minutes into the second half.

Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

Those raft of changes from Mikel Arteta at half-time have seen just four of their starting XI remain on the pitch; Kepa, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri.

Arsenal have a corner early on in this second half as Vieira’s shot from distance deflects behind. The delivery from the left has too much on it, going over the heads of all the Arsenal players in the box, and Betis are able to clear.

Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

Arsenal are closing in on the signing of Newcastle and Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes in a deal worth £75m. He has been given permission to undergo a medical today and is set to join Arsenal in the coming days. One midfielder coming into Arsenal is set to see another depart as Dane Christian Norgaard closes in on a move to Everton after just one season at Arsenal.

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#1908. ‘I felt my leg…’ – Dominik Szoboszlai makes worrying injury admission after Hungary win

Dominik Szoboszlai has given an update on his knee injury after Hungary’s win over Georgia on Saturday, and his comments could be quite concerning for Liverpool fans.

The midfielder’s involvement for his country during this international window was placed in doubt after the knock that he incurred in the Reds’ victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, although he still linked up with Marco Rossi’s squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures.

The Hungarian FA had deferred any decision on whether the 26-year-old would play until the last minute, but he featured for the entirety of his nation’s 2-0 triumph in Tbilisi and claimed the assist for Barnabas Varga’s clinching goal.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he nearly pulled out of playing after he felt a twinge during the warm-up prior to kick-off, but his determination to feature would eventually prevail.

In quotes relayed by Nemzeti Sport, the Hungary captain said: “I was always 100% sure that I would be able to play, but the doctors were less sure. I progressed day by day, focused on myself, received treatment.

“I played with my leg for a training session and a half, and in the warm-up I was close to cancelling it because I felt my leg on one of the shots, but if I’ve come this far, I won’t let the team down. Now the treatment starts all over again. I have to be ready again by Tuesday.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Szoboszlai’s comments may well come as a worry to Liverpool fans, with the midfielder admitting that he played through the pain barrier and seemingly defied the assessment of medical professionals.

His remark about getting ready for Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night will also have Andoni Iraola sweating, with the 26-year-old set to push himself for a tight turnaround even though he seems nowhere near full fitness.

It’s natural that, as captain of his country, the Reds’ number 8 will stop at nothing to try and be available for them, but his club will be left praying that he comes through the Magyars’ next game unscathed.

Szoboszlai will return from international duty into a hectic run of 11 Liverpool fixtures before the end of December, and we’ll need him and his teammates to be operating at their best throughout that busy period.

For everyone at Anfield, Hungary’s match on Tuesday will be monitored with frayed nerves to see if the midfielder comes through without any further complications in his knee.

#1904. ‘Looking back…’ – Alexander Isak speaks out over penalty controversy in defeat to Arsenal

Alexander Isak has spoken out about the controversial penalty incident in which he was involved during Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal a fortnight ago.

Five minutes after Kai Havertz netted the only goal of the match, the Reds’ number 9 had his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber inside the box, but neither on-field referee Andy Madley nor Stuart Attwell on VAR deemed it to have been a foul.

The transgression was unmistakably clear on replays, and the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel has since acknowledged that a spot kick should’ve been awarded.

Speaking to reporters whilst on international duty with Sweden, Isak was asked if he felt that he should’ve had a penalty.

He replied (Aftonbladet, via Liverpool Echo): “Yeah, looking back I suppose it does look that way, but when you’re in the moment, you don’t always perceive exactly what’s happening.

“I could feel myself being pulled a bit, but not to the extent that it appears later on. I was focused on scoring. It’s hard to try to score and then fall down at the same time. I was so locked in on the goal that I didn’t really register it.”

On whether he should’ve gone to ground to try and sway the referee, Isak said: “I don’t think there’s any need to embellish or go down on purpose. Sure, if I’d had a better read on the situation, I might have made sure the referee noticed it, that’s about all you can do, but I don’t believe you need to dive or exaggerate in situations like this.

“Perhaps it shouldn’t even matter that much, given that we have VAR and systems in place to make the decisive calls in these kinds of moments.”

Isak is absolutely right in saying that a penalty should’ve been awarded, and that he shouldn’t have to act unnaturally to convince the referee to give the decision in his team’s favour.

Andoni Iraola remarked after the game that a spot kick probably would’ve been given if the Liverpool striker had gone to ground, but the onus isn’t on players to sway the officials – it’s on the latter to get these big calls right, especially with recourse to VAR.

It feels as though the debate about officiating in the Premier League will continue indefinitely, with no discernible sign of an improvement in standards from Pro Ref figurehead Howard Webb.

It’s to Isak’s great credit that he’s given such a calm and measured verdict on the penalty incident when he and his team were so blatantly wronged. He’d have had every right to complain profusely about what happened; we’d suspect that many other players would’ve done so if they were in that situation.

He certainly hasn’t let it bother him in terms of his contributions on the pitch, with the 27-year-old scoring in Liverpool’s subsequent games against Fenerbahce and Crystal Palace to take his tally for the season to eight goals in 14 matches across all competitions.

That is, in fact, the best response to the injustice which was done against him Anfield two weeks ago.

#1900. Inside the world of Captain Chaos at Man United: Michael Carrick will not walk away but here's what the players are saying as they fail to respond to his direction, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 10 November 2026

While the Manchester United fans who had gone ahead with a booze boycott of Old Trafford watched in horror as their team teetered on the brink of total collapse and head coach Michael Carrick clung to his job, you couldn't help but think of Lloyd Bridges as Steve McCroskey, the frazzled air traffic control boss in Airplane! 'Looks like I picked the wrong week to quit drinking!'

God knows United have forced their supporters to hit the bottle this season, not least in the past six days when they have handed a two-goal advantage to Roma and Aston Villa (twice) and still managed to salvage a win and a draw.

But this cannot carry on. As cavalier as United like to be, this is not the way to play football.

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, it's great for the Sky Sports cameras beaming it live and the Amazon Prime documentary makers filming behind the scenes, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch.

Nowhere in the UEFA coaching manuals will you find a chapter on routinely conceding the first two goals being a sensible route to success. For all his bluster after a bonkers 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Carrick knows it and his players know it.

'After we concede goals we show character, but if we do this before we can win much more games,' said Matheus Cunha. 'I don't know why, everyone tries to get answers for that. We want to be the best and show that we can come back. We need to show the mentality to do this from the start.'

As Manchester United head coach, Michael Carrick is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch

It isn't just in the last week either. United were a goal down against Atletico Madrid inside the first minute and Como in the second. They were two down to Villa after three minutes and 40 seconds, the earliest that has happened to United in the Premier League era.

This is not a coincidence. It is not bad luck. This is in the mind-set of these Manchester United players, and the game management of Carrick – and that is what should worry Old Trafford bosses the most.

As if being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks after a start of one win from 10 games – the worst since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago – is not bad enough, United don't seem to be playing to a plan. They are not responding to direction. They are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails.

Carrick made reference to it when he spoke before this game, admitting that the players are better when they don't think too much.

'Momentum within games, day-to-day, week-to-week, game-to-game, it's huge,' he said at Carrington on Friday. 'I think it's important with your feelings and your emotions to roll with it. Then your memory can click in and you realise, 'Oh yeah, this is what it feels like, this is how it should be', and you start seeing different things.

'It's all got to come together, but feeling, confidence, and that emotion and sometimes not even thinking. You're at your best when you don't think too much and you just trust and play on instinct, and I think we did a lot of that the other night (against Roma).'

The irony is that Carrick was so measured, so composed as a player. Now, as coach, he is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos. United's games are reminiscent of the high-scoring madness of Erik ten Hag's last full season in charge, devoid of stability or structure.

That is what Carrick's employers need to consider when they sit down to discuss whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge which guided the club towards third place and Champions League qualification.

Now they are third from bottom and will stay in the relegation zone for the duration of the international break. For three minutes on Sunday, Manchester United – the aristocrats of English football – were actually in last place after Sunderland took the lead against Chelsea and Crystal Palace were still goalless with Liverpool.

United don't seem to be playing to a plan or responding to direction - they are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails

Carrick's employers need to consider  whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge

That being in 18th place – one below Coventry – is somehow seen as blessed relief from the unrelenting humiliation of this season, says everything about the state of the club.

At the end of a week that marked 40 years since Ferguson's arrival and was celebrated by a dinner with many of his most famous players, it has been quite the fall from grace.

Which brings us back to the fans. They are a loyal bunch and once again serenaded Carrick off the pitch at full-time having spent much of the previous two hours slaughtering the owners, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Protest groups had urged them to boycott buying alcohol at the stadium to hit the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in the pocket. 'Your funeral not ours – sell up now,' read one new banner. 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners,' said another.

But they know their football at United. Was it support or just sympathy with a head coach who has done his best in an impossible situation?

Carrick says he won't walk away and they never do. On Remembrance Sunday, he stood there on the touchline with a poppy on his arm and hope in his heart that United could get themselves out of another self-inflicted crisis.

They did. Again. But how much longer can United and Carrick keep winging it, and believe that calm will emerge from the chaos.
