#1840. Dave Challinor pleased to see Sheffield Wednesday players speaking his language in Plymouth Argyle win

After starting his time as Owls manager with consecutive cup defeats, Challinor won the one that mattered most, beating League One promotion rivals Plymouth Argyle 3-0 at Hillsborough to move into the League One play-off places.

In truth, the Owls were poor in the first half but where Argyle missed their chances, they did not, taking the lead with a deflected strike from Billy Mitchell, his first goal since 2021.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

And they were better in the second half without being sparkling, adding goals from Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard.

It left Challinor with areas to work on as well as three points.

"Okay," was his verdict when asked what he made of the performance. "I think we've got loads to do.

“To come here, score three goals, keep a clean sheet, at times maybe luck more than judgement, certainly in the first half, with some of the opportunities we gave away, it is amazing.

"I think you look at the first half and I was really open with the players and asked them what they thought.

"Sometimes it takes 10 minutes to earn the right (to play), sometimes it takes 60 minutes, sometimes you never earn the right.

"Plymouth are really good at asking questions of you, and in the first half I don't think we've dealt with them questions well enough at times, and maybe need to compete better and win first contacts and drop on second balls and track runners and probably got away with it a little bit at times. They were really honest about that and said that was the case.

"The second half was much, much better. I thought we dealt with their threats and then we were able to make the game look a little bit more like what we'd want it to look like.

"It shows, again, the importance of set pieces at any level, but especially at this level, to score from them too.

As for what his message was at the interval, Challinor said: "Exactly the same as at the start of the game, you have to compete, you have to outrun, you'd love to outplay, we want to try and smooth things out if we can, but you're playing against a team every single week that's trying to stop you do what you might want to do, and sometimes the game doesn't look like you want it to look like.

"With that being the case, find a way. I think it's a big saying around the football club and around the city, find a way to dig in and win in certain ways.

"If you can win it in every different way, then as a football team, you're in a really good place. We'd all love it to look a certain way, but we're not entitled enough to think that's ever going to be the case.

"So it was, can we still do the things we need to do better, compete and win second balls, and then can we have a composure, come down some levels to try and play the game, or play the game in a manner that what we wanted it to look like?"

Keillor-Dunn's goal was his sixth in nine appearances and, after a prolific first haf of last season at Barnsley, Challinor revealed he is working on ways to maximise the forward's output.

"We did some work with Davo and some of the other forwards around their scoring capacity over the last five seasons. You look at Kyle Whopton, who's the top scorer in the league. Davo's outscored Woots in terms of goals in the last five seasons and without giving too much away, where Davo scores his goals are all very similar.

"I just felt he'd spent too much time, not in them areas, too much time in wide areas. He's the best finisher we've got at the club. He's lethal when he gets in, apart from the chance he had about five minutes before he did score.

"So we need to get him in there more, we need to keep him in the middle of the pitch, we need to keep him in the box, we need to service it and put balls in where he might not score from the first contact but he's lethal and clinical from second balls that drop.

"The goal that he scored is his type of goal, a drop down, drop on a second ball and a really good finish."

#1839. Ex-Premier League ref calls Mikel Arteta a ‘nightmare’ to deal with

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has named Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as the toughest person to deal with on the touchline.

Last month, Arteta received his second yellow card of the season during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton but said after the game that he had a dossier of other managers committing similar offences which have gone unpunished.

The Arsenal manager now faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives a third yellow card.

Scott, who refereed in the Premier League for a decade before retiring in 2025, claims Arteta ‘does push all the limits all of the time’ and described the Spaniard as ‘hard work’.

When asked who was the worst manager to deal with on the touchline, Scott told The Athletic: ‘Well, the trite answer is all of them when they’re losing.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The honest answer, I’m afraid, I know whatever I say at this point just gets me pelters but it is Arteta. He is the hardest work.

‘He really does push all the limits all of the time. I don’t mind that in many ways, he’s trying to get a competitive advantage for his team. That’s fine. That’s part of his job. And of course, he’s entitled to do it, and it’s for us to place them, but he does make your life extremely difficult.

‘He’s out of his box [technical area] all the time. I watched him recently in the game against Everton and every time Everton had the ball anywhere near the touchline on his side, he was like joining in the press, his toes are on the touchline.

‘As fourth official, it’s a nightmare, because if you step forward and do anything about it, you’re being pedantic, being petty. He does get away with rather too much. The officials do need to be a bit tighter. And I was one of them who let him do that. I’m not going to deny that. But he was just hard work. Really, really hard work all the time in a way that others tended to be hard work some of the time.

#1835. What Tom Brady's exit means for Birmingham City: Why NFL legend quit St Andrew's, 'body coach' Alex Guerrero's future role revealed - and impact on Knighthead's ambitious £2bn plans for Premier League push and new stadium

Published: 08:41 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 11:15 EST, 10 November 2026

Tom Brady has quit Birmingham but his influence will continue to be felt around the Championship leaders through one of his closest allies.

The club announced via a social media post late on Monday that the NFL legend’s three-year association with Blues would end.

Titled ‘Tom Brady Departure’, the 62-word statement read: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

'It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’

Yet it can be revealed that the ideas of Brady’s ‘body coach’ Alex Guerrero will continue to inform Blues’ push for Premier League football.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the reasons for Brady’s departure – and what the future holds for Blues now he has gone...

Tom Brady (right) has left Birmingham City - though their plans remain ambitious under owners Knighthead and chairman Tom Wagner (left)

Brady brought stardust with him to Birmingham and was the figurehead of a new era at the club - despite attending just four matches since buying into Blues

Brady has not been a visible presence in Birmingham for about two years and attended only four matches after he was unveiled as a ‘minority investor’ in 2023, not long after US investors Knighthead had completed their takeover.

It has proved challenging for Brady to divide his time between Birmingham and his commitments in the US, where he has a £280million contract as Fox Sports main NFL analyst. He has also been part-owner of the Las Vegas Raiders since 2024.

Daily Mail Sport understands, however, that Guerrero’s methods will still be used at Blues – a significant detail given his long-term association with Brady.

Described by Brady as his 'body coach', the pair have worked together for two decades and Brady credits Guerrero with extending his NFL career beyond his 45th birthday. With Guerrero at his side, Brady won four Super Bowls and three MVP (Most Valuable Player) awards.

Birmingham chiefs have been very impressed with Guerrero, who they believe has transformed the club’s approach to fitness and recovery.

Since Guerrero came in with Brady, recovery sessions the day after a game have been mandatory and players have had individual conditioning programmes, including tailored advice on nutrition.

Daily Mail Sport understands the methods of Brady's 'body coach' Alex Guerrero (left) will still be used at Blues

In 2025, skipper Christoph Klarer told Daily Mail Sport: ‘We have so many physios and massage therapists who show you exercises in the gym and treat you before and after training. There will always be a physio available at the training ground if I want to see one. That’s not typical.’

Klarer and fellow defender Phil Neumann have not missed a game through injury as Blues players since joining in 2024 and 2025 respectively.

There have been subtle changes, though. Many of the logos and messages from TBRx – Brady’s performance and fitness company – have disappeared from the walls of the training ground in rural Warwickshire. They will be replaced by branding for the recently-launched ‘Keep Right On’ initiative as well as messages that boss Chris Davies believes are particularly relevant to his squad.

At this stage, certainly not. Knighthead remain determined to push forward their vision for Blues, with the £2billion Sports Quarter project at its heart.

The centrepiece of the Sports Quarter is the Powerhouse – a 62,000-seat stadium development that Blues hope will be one of the best in the country.

Blues may have lost their most famous face but all indications are that Brady’s departure is not a sign of Knighthead scaling back their commitment. The US group still believe Birmingham can become one of England’s most prominent clubs and are hugely excited by their progress this term, with Davies’ men top of the Championship heading into the November international break.

Knighthead still believe Birmingham can become one of England’s most prominent clubs and are hugely excited by their progress this term

Chris Davies’ men are top of the Championship heading into the November international break

It is easy to categorise Brady as a mere figurehead but that would be unfair. The 2025 Amazon Prime docuseries Built In Birmingham: Brady & The Blues was streamed in about 200 countries. There is no doubt that Brady’s presence helped Blues push certain transfer deals over the line, with Brady conducting video calls with targets. Earlier this season, Davies was late for a press conference because he had been on the phone to Brady.

The 49-year-old had a good relationship with the squad, too. He developed a strong rapport with former Blues forward Alfie May and even appeared on a FaceTime call during the wedding of May’s brother.

Equally, it would be unwise to exaggerate Brady’s role. If Blues win promotion this term, it will be a combination of Knighthead’s investment and the work of Davies and his players. By elevating the club’s profile globally, perhaps Brady has already done his job. Now it is time for the class of 2026 to write their own story.

During the early part of Brady’s time at St Andrew’s, the club leaned heavily into their rivalry with Wrexham, who are owned by Hollywood star Ryan Reynolds and his fellow actor Rob McElhenney.

When Blues took on Wrexham in September 2024, their 3-1 win was almost a sideshow. As well as the three famous Americans, David Beckham was also at St Andrew’s. When the clubs met, the US stars traded friendly insults before and after the match, generating a great deal of attention on social media.

David Beckham (right) was among the famous faces to take in a Birmingham game alongside Brady

Knighthead remain determined to push forward their vision for Blues, with the £2billion Sports Quarter project at its heart. The centrepiece is the Powerhouse – a 62,000-seat stadium

There was less of this when Blues won 2-1 at Wrexham earlier this season and perhaps that was no coincidence. There have certainly been those at Blues who feel that, at times, the club bought into the Wrexham rivalry a little too much and that forging their own path might be more fruitful.

There is no suggestion that Brady pushed the links with Wrexham yet if he is no longer associated with Blues, they may decline naturally.

In Brady’s first season, Blues were relegated to League One, with the NFL star admitting the club had tried to change too much, too soon. The appointment of Wayne Rooney was the highest-profile of those errors.

Brady departs with the club as healthy as it has been for some time. Even if he was rarely central to that recovery, he deserves at least some of the credit for it.

#1833. Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed ban for tackle that led to Jesus de Miguel death

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement said: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Speaking this week, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said that Owono is still considering his future in football.

‘He is deeply affected by the situation,’ Manso said.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’

Earlier this week, Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Owono is barely leaving his house following De Miguel’s death and is closely working with psychologists and doctors.

The win pushed Lindsey’s men into fourth in the League Two table, level on points with third-placed Grimsby Town.

#1830. Wigan Athletic 2 Barnsley FC 1: Game management kills Reds for umpteenth time this season

In the event, it was Wigan - as Barnsley’s propensity to not do their jobs from a defensive perspective in the second half resurfaced into their most important game of the campaign thus far against fellow strugglers.

Barnsley, for seemingly the umpteenth time in 2026-27, were in the contest, with Cameron McGeehan’s ninth goal of the season on 57 minutes cancelling out Fraser Murray’s 36th-minute opener.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

And then they spoiled it with a rotten concession on 75 minutes, scored by Jensen Weir, to settle this six-pointer, with keeper Ciaran Slicker and left-back Ziyad Larkeche both being culpable.

It extended the Reds’ winless sequence at league level to a rough nine games. This was their fifth successive away loss in the third tier on the spin.

A nice side at times, but also a naive one, they sadly always give their opponents a chance. Somewhere along the line.

Barnsley were comfortable enough for most of the first half, but failing to cope with a mini spell of pressure as their opponents cranked up the gas proved to be their undoing - and in many respects it has been the story of their season.

Murray had delivered a warning a few minutes earlier with his sweet curler producing a full-stretch parry from the well-positioned Slicker.

A few minutes later, the Reds custodian had no chance when Murray again showed delicious technique to bend an unstoppable low shot into the far corner, for his first goal of the campaign. An important one.

How the ball arrived at his feet, with Wigan afforded an ocean of space in the middle of the pitch was poor from a Reds perspective.

Wigan fancied it on the flanks against Jubril Okedina and Larkeche, with their number 10s in Brad Burrowes and Jon Mellish becoming more of a force as the half progressed.

Larkeche was cautioned in a first half which also saw Barnsley captain Cam McGeechan pick up a costly booking which will mean he misses the home derby with Sheffield Wednesday - after amassing five league yellows this term.

The Reds made three changes from their last league game against Oxford United a fortnight ago, with Daniel Johnson handed a first league start.

Okedina started in place of the suspended Jack Shepherd in the heart of defence, while Makenzie Kirk got the nod up two following his brace in midweek.

Tobi Adeyemo was not in the match-day squad, with Patrick Kelly on international duty with Northern Ireland.

Reyes Cleary displayed the sporadic threat in the first period for Barnsley. Wigan were wary of him, but Barnsley looked toothless otherwise.

Their best moment came with a well-struck free-kick from Luca Connell, which was tipped over by Latics keeper Joe Whitworth.

Barnsley string one or two nice bits of play together in open play - particularly down the sides - but possessed little threat where it hurts against a Latics backline who did look susceptible.

The first chance on the resumption was a home one, but Mellish scuffed his effort when well-placed.

Stendel moved Johnson further forward in the second period, with McGeehan dropping in.

Wigan were happy enough to let Barnsley have the ball, while picking their times to press and pounce, given the fact they did not need to chase the game.

The visitors were increasingly in need of something and thankfully it arrived.

Moments after Amani Richards and Rylan Brownlie entered the fray, the Reds were level.

Connell found Cleary and he expertly manufactured space before fizzing over a superb low cross which was buried by McGeehan. It was classic wing-play from Cleary.

At the other end, Slicker had to be alert to race out and deny Christian Saydee.

The importance of a winner did not need to be spelt out to both sides. Barnsley showed promise, but needed to be mindful of their game management going the other way.

Morgan Fox was afforded too much space on the left and his cross was attacked at the back post by Weir, who got above Larkeche far too easily, with matters compounded by Slicker’s unconvincing attempt to keep out the header.

Burrowes went close to a killer third as Wigan smelt blood. Two was enough.

Wigan Athletic: Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett (Trevitt 68), Weir, Power, Mellish; Burrowes (Miller 87), Murray; Saydee (Hogan 67). Substitutes unused: J Walsh, Chilokoa-Mullen, A Harris, Higgins.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche (Reid ); Connell, Johnson (Richards 56); Yoganathan, McGeehan (Noslin 82), Cleary; Kirk (Brownlie 56). Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, Smith, Alker.

Daniele Massaro has spoken about how much Franco Baresi meant to him, and how much he now misses the AC Milan icon.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

“Camarda hasn’t found the playing time he himself hoped for. The club certainly continues to have faith in Camarda, but I can confirm that Milan’s intention is to let Camarda go in January,” the journalist revealed.

“The idea is that he can try a new experience to grow, get playing time, and demonstrate his qualities. Milan have made the decision. Then we’ll see if things change between now and January. Anything can happen in football… maybe he scores three goals in a row and the situation changes.

“But as of now, Milan have decided to let Camarda go in January. For this reason, the club is already looking at other forwards, beyond Tresoldi; there are also other names on the list of the club on Via Aldo Rossi [the club’s headquarters].”

#1824. The numbers suggest Chelsea are pushovers as they slide down the Premier League table... and club legend GUS POYET says it's time to prove they're up for a fight

Published: 07:38 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Morgan Rogers insisted it was no intentional drive-by. That he did not mean to knee Trai Hume in the head while the Sunderland defender was sitting up after a foul. Just an accident, honest.

The history shared between these two particular players opened the incident to interpretation.

Hume had folded Rogers like a deckchair in a 1-1 draw for Aston Villa last season. The challenge went viral. Sunderland shared it on their social media, glamourising it. Rogers responded at the time by saying: 'Great message to send out. Dangerous tackles getting highlight reels.'

At the Stadium of Light on Sunday, Hume was starting to sit up when Rogers caught him. Chelsea were losing 1-0, and frustrated. Their £117million arrival from Villa apologised immediately, so we will believe him when he says it was an innocent collision rather than retribution.

Nevertheless, Rogers does have an aggressive side to him. He squared up with Declan Rice at Arsenal, and James Tarkowski at Everton, and was signed in the summer partially for that passion.

Rogers has contested more duels than any other Chelsea player this season. He loses more than he wins, but is involved, for better or worse. He is Xabi Alonso's most-fouled footballer, while nobody has committed more fouls than this 6ft 2in England international.

Morgan Rogers (right) showed some fight during Chelsea's loss at Sunderland that appears to be lacking across the whole squad

If Rogers' team-mates showed the same mentality they may have avoided defeat on Sunday

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso needs his side to develop an aggressive streak

So when we ponder whether Alonso's Chelsea are pushovers, Rogers is arguably an exception. He is a hard nut surrounded by a soft shell, and that was a problem at Sunderland.

It was not only that Brian Brobbey bullied Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Regis Le Bris' side were all at it, a team of bouncers ready to rough up the lads planning to party. Cole Palmer and Co ended up getting tossed out of the Stadium of Light on their rears. Chelsea recorded 69 per cent possession - their highest of the Premier League season so far - but were second-best throughout.

Gus Poyet saw that. He played for Chelsea, managed Sunderland, and was an assistant to Dennis Wise at Leeds, who will be the next visitors to Stamford Bridge after this international break.

Daniel Farke's side have won more duels and aerial duels than any other Premier League team this season, which, given what we witnessed on Sunday, should be a concern for Alonso.

Poyet can predict what is coming. Chelsea-Leeds is already a fixture with a narrative attached. It never needs a second invitation to be talked up as 'dirty'. Alonso's side will need to show a willingness to compete if that awaits, more than they managed when travelling to Sunderland.

'Sunderland went to the game with that old-fashioned mentality,' the 58-year-old Uruguayan told Daily Mail Sport. 'Pressure from the fans, noise, tackling, "I'm gonna run over you". Chelsea went on to try to play. There was quite a big difference in that aggression. We see teams that are looking so much for an identity that they forget the process to win games.'

Poyet brought up Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton last month. We told him how Alonso had admitted it was his favourite performance of the season, describing it as 'solid' and 'serious'.

'There you go,' said Poyet, who thinks before travelling to the Stadium of Light, it would have been worth showing Chelsea's players videos from that victory at the Hill Dickinson. It was a rare showing of seriousness from Alonso's side. Only David Moyes' Everton, with 83, have committed fewer fouls than Chelsea's 95 in the Premier League this season. While giving away free-kicks is hardly a cause for celebration, it is not the worst way of measuring whether you are there to push or be pushed.

Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey (left) bulled Chelsea's Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana (right)

'For me that was a proper old-fashioned game, being able to win like that,' Poyet said about Chelsea's win at Everton. 'Put the video on and say, "Play the same".

'Now I know what the other side are going to say after watching the Sunderland game. Leeds will be saying, 'Let's go'. Leeds are very solid, and very aggressive, so it can be that kind of game.

'More and more, through the years, I think from the pandemic to now, the difference between the teams is mental. Identity, positions, shapes, blah, blah, blah, but when they are right in here (in the head), it's big. Right now, Leeds, as a team, are a little ahead mentally.'

Alonso is a polite manager. Given the chance to have a pop at the refereeing at the Stadium of Light - how Chelsea were not awarded a penalty when Cole Palmer was sandwiched, but Sunderland were when Brobbey dropped down in front of Colwill - he declined. The Blues boss chose instead to decry his team's defending as substandard. Colwill was hooked at half-time, while there were two new summer signings in the back line in Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria who need to get to grips with the Premier League, sooner rather than later.

Poyet's first appearance after signing for Chelsea in 1997 was in the Charity Shield. Roy Keane welcomed him to English football with a kick to the head - with a little less subtlety than Rogers' knee on Hume. It finished 1-1 before Manchester United won on penalties.

Ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet has warned them of the threat Leeds pose later this month

Poyet learned a harsh lesson in that match, and not only from Keane's high kick. 'I couldn't get in the pace of the game,' Poyet recalls. 'I was always late. Ruud (Gullit) at half-time told me, "Gus, you're not really in the front, not really at the back". I said, "I'm trying!" The game was too fast.'

In a weird way, an ACL injury suffered by Poyet helped. He used the recovery time to prepare for returning. 'I went to the stadium, I was watching, learning the language, listening to Dennis Wise in the dressing room, getting that mentality,' he said. 'Then when I came back, I knew everything.

'That was my mentality. Some players need time. Some adjust quickly. You need to use all the time. For example, use this game against Sunderland when you play against Leeds. You cannot say, 'We didn't expect it'. Expect it! It's going to be similar.'

#1823. ‘Next star’ – Mauricio Pochettino tipped to sign £67m target for Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino has been tipped to complete the marquee signing of Como midfielder Nico Paz for Manchester United.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half year deal in Manchester and will join up with the squad ahead of their trip to Anfield to face Liverpool next Sunday.

United have made their worst start to a season in 40 years, and are currently without a league win since mid-August.

As he looks to arrest that slide, Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as United look to fill gaping holes in their squad at left-back and forward areas.

But former Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor believes Pochettino may also look to move on senior players and earmarked Bruno Fernandes as one who might have an uncertain future under the Argentine.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Fernandes’ contract is up at the end of the season, with recent reports suggesting that the Red Devils captain has rejected a second contract offer from the club.

And speaking on talkSPORT, Agbonlahor mused: ‘Maybe Pochettino comes in and says, “You know what? I don’t like his attitude. I don’t like the way he throws his arms up at his teammates, the way he threw Michael Carrick under the bus. Can I go and get my own players?”‘

Should Fernandes leave the club, Agbonlahor earmarked Como midfielder Paz as the perfect candidate to ‘refresh’ United’s squad.

‘Nico Paz – how good has he been?’ he added. ‘He’s the next star for Argentina.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Does Pochettino say, “You know what? I want him next summer from Como, make it happen”. Save the money on wages that maybe Bruno Fernandes wants.

‘So he might have his own ideas to get all these players out that maybe have been a little bit of a problem and to refresh the whole squad.’

Paz tormented Michael Carrick’s side in the Champions League last month, scoring twice and providing an assist in a 4-1 victory, having grown into one of Serie A’s brightest talents under Cesc Fabregas.

The Argentine joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid, although Los Blancos do retain a £67million buy-back clause, which can be activated next summer.

Recent reports in Spain indicate that the possibility of a move to the Premier League appeals to Paz’s representatives, although Como’s transfer position and Real’s intentions will be a deciding factor.

#1822. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

Enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

There will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

Clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

Jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

Yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

Understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

Couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

Just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

Manchester United make three changes – Tynan Thompson, Toby Collyer and Dan Armer replace Santos, Heaven and Dorgu.

And for Senne Lammens, a new shirt number, from 31 to Numero Uno:

Lammens is not the only one. Marcus Rashford wore 39 in his debut season with Man Utd, moved to 19 for the next three then changed to 10 when Zlatan Ibrahimovic left the club. The 10 shirt has been given to Matheus Cunha so now he will wear 14, the number he had at Barcelona in his Liga title-winning season.

If you’re watching in the UK, the match is live on ITV. A friendly! Live on ITV.  That’s Croke Park for you.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1821. ‘It changes everything’ – Zidane welcomes Mbappe injury return

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Zinedine Zidane believes Kylian Mbappe's return from injury "changes everything" as France prepare for a crucial Nations League clash against Turkiye.

Mbappe was sidelined with a hamstring injury during France's 3-1 defeat to Italy on Thursday, swinging Group A1 wide open ahead of the final games.

The defeat, which was Zidane's first since taking over from Didier Deschamps, leaves France second in the group ahead of hosting Turkiye, with leaders Italy travelling to third-place Belgium on Sunday.

Victory for France would guarantee a spot in the quarter-finals, and Mbappe's return gives Les Bleus a timely boost.

The Real Madrid forward scored the only goal in the reverse fixture against Turkiye, though he missed the other three fixtures during the previous international break through injury.

"It changes everything; we prefer to have him than not have him," said Zidane on Mbappe's injury return.

"There's no problem, he'll be with us. You'll see how we play. These are coaching matters.

"They are all normally available. But we have to wait for the last training session. But all the players are available to train.

"We know what we did in Italy. We did some good things, but when you lose, there are things that didn't go so well.

"Even if a point is enough, our objective is always to win the match. We'll have to play a great match."

There have been rumours that Zidane's relationship with Mbappe has soured recently, but the 54-year-old was quick to brush those off.

"I don't understand, but it's not a big deal," he said of the rumours. "That's why I'm not going to get into the debate.

"I have the relationship of a coach with his player, and it's going perfectly. I can't stop people from saying what's being said. But it's nonsense. It's a shame and quite annoying."

#1820. Erling Haaland speaks out on Manchester City future as financial scandal rumbles on

Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Manchester City’s players have not said much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, says he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything.’

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’

#1819. Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after criticism from Liverpool legend

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness said on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Declan Rice hit TWO worldie free-kicks vs Real Madrid 🤯So nice he did it twice ✌️ pic.twitter.com/zg5CzlQQNh

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

#1818. Romano and Moretto provide update on Milan’s Endrick pursuit: “Hasn’t said no”

This week, there have been some interesting rumours about AC Milan and their pursuit of Endrick. However, it may have been a bit misleading.

Yesterday, it seemed that Milan were almost out of the race to sign Endrick, with the Brazilian against the club’s Devil logo. Instead, the Corriere dello Sport report would have you believe that he’d prefer a move to Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, his agency have denied this rumour and later reports suggested that the Rossoneri are very much in the race to sign the Brazilian. In fact, he could even leave Real Madrid permanently – with future clauses – so things have certainly developed a bit this week.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Romano provided an update on Endrick’s situation alongside Matteo Moretto and their words have been relayed by MilanNews.

“Endrick is currently evaluating his future. On one side, Real Madrid doesn’t want to release him, from the president to Jose Mourinho, who continues to reiterate this publicly; on the other, the boy wants to play,” Romano started.

“I wanted to add a footnote: Endrick’s entourage, ROC Nation, are letting it be known that the player hasn’t said no to Milan; he hasn’t said no to anyone on November 12th. He’s still in the evaluation phase; we’ll see what happens.

“He has two months left with Real Madrid: football changes in five minutes. Endrick’s position is currently completely open, and he’s a player—we were the first to talk about him—that Milan really likes. But it’s true that Roma is also there, there’s a queue of many teams ready to chase him.

“I just wanted to clarify that Endrick hasn’t said no to Milan. He’s keeping everything open while waiting to figure out—if he leaves—the best solution.”

Moretto then added, “A lot will depend on the player. In December, he’ll really understand what kind of path he wants to take. He’s currently noticing this lack of playing time, so the loan option is taking shape. Roma have been maintaining contact for weeks.

“Roma want an additional striker because they believe with one or two signings they can really compete for something important this year. Keep an eye on Roma, but Milan was one of the first to move, and the relationship between Cardinale and ROC Nation is excellent. So far, Roma has maintained contact a little more actively, but Milan is insisting.”

It’s clear that January will be very interesting where Endrick is involved, especially with him being the one to make the decisions on his future.

#1817. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of Man Utd mission

Mauricio Pochettino would welcome the chance to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares for the task of resurrecting Manchester United.

Michael Carrick’s successor’s penultimate match in charge of United States ended in an emphatic 6-0 thrashing of Haiti as he moved a step closer to beginning his United tenure.

The former Tottenham boss will start life at the Red Devils on Wednesday after two Nations League matches with Haiti, but USA all but assured their place in the semi-finals of the competition with a comprehensive first-leg showing.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The 54-year-old will have little time to reflect on his accomplishments in his soon-to-be former role as he will immediately begin plotting for his first game in charge of United at Anfield next Sunday.

Pochettino inherits a side that is currently in the bottom three in the Premier League table, short on confidence and a dressing room split following the recent actions of senior players, including the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez.

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’

#1815. Bruno Fernandes gives Man Utd Mauricio Pochettino ultimatum over new contract

Bruno Fernandes will delay any decision on a new Manchester United contract until he has made up his mind on new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The 32-year-old’s current deal expires at the end of the season, although the club has an option to extend his contract by another year.

With Fernandes already rejecting two offers of a new deal, the Red Devils are expected to trigger the 12-month extension to avoid him agreeing a move abroad on a free transfer, which he would be able to do in the last six months of his contract.

The Sun report that Manchester United remain confident Fernandes will sign a new contract, but that his decision is based on how things play out under new boss Pochettino.

The Portuguese star has cut a frustrated figure so far this season under Michael Carrick, playing well below his capabilities as the whole team has struggled.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Carrick has been axed and Pochettino returns to the Premier League for a fourth job, having managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

Not only is Fernandes waiting to see what working under the Argentine is like, but also whether the hierarchy will back the new boss in the transfer market.

The Red Devils signed Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos over the summer, but failed to strengthen at the back or up front.

The midfield has been revamped, but United look very short at full-back and centre-forward, while they are well stocked at centre-back, but their options continue to perform poorly.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

If Fernandes is to remain at Old Trafford beyond this season, he will have to see some intent in the transfer market from the decision-makers at the club.

Like Fernandes, Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire see their current deals expire in the summer of 2027 but the club can extend them by another year. Big decisions are to be made on both.

Luke Shaw is also into the final few months of his current contract, with the experienced left-back currently sidelined with injury.

Work on the squad will begin in the winter transfer window, with Pochettino arriving to take charge next week after finishing his time in charge of USA.

Speaking of his choice to leave America for Manchester, he said: ‘It’s difficult to talk now. I’m a very emotional guy. It’s a very sad decision.

‘But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true.

#1814. The little-known new face called up by England: Can you name the star brought in to replace Ezri Konsa?

Published: 05:58 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has made a first-time England call-up to replace Ezri Konsa - but casual fans could be forgiven if they do not recognise the latest Three Lions addition.

He is not a widely-recognised face among the stars from the Premier League and other top European leagues in Tuchel's selection but James Hill, 24, has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose this season.

The central defender, who started his career at Fleetwood Town, has enjoyed a dream few months: He married partner Tara Rose in June, welcomed his first child in August and has now had his maiden England call.

England announced today that Arsenal defender Konsa will not be in contention to face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night - although he will be fit to potentially face Spain away on Sunday - and Hill has been called up in his place.

Hill has played for England's Under 20s and Under 21s but this is his first senior call. He was signed by Bournemouth for just £1.2million in 2022 - beating Sheffield United, Burnley, Leeds, Southampton, Tottenham and even Barcelona, who all checked on his progress.

Bournemouth's official X account posted today: 'Congratulations, Hilly. Our defender has earned a first senior @England call-up.'

James Hill - pictured with new wife Tara - has been called up to the latest England squad (Source: Instagram/james_hill_10)

Hill has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose

Hill's route to the top is a fascinating one. He attended a trial day at Fleetwood as a 14-year-old and managed to impress them enough to earn place at their new academy.

Interestingly, Hill did not play for a football team of any kind before he was 10, simply kicking a ball around with friends and playing in the garden to hone his skills.

Blackpool opted against signing him after a trial and he was then dropped by Bolton after a short stint.

It proved to be a shrewd piece of talent identification from Fleetwood, with Hill later becoming the club's record sale, eclipsing the fee they received for Jamie Vardy.

And having signed for the Cherries in 2022, Hill has now established himself as a key member of Marco Rose's side.

He's played every minute of every Premier League match this season at the heart of the defence and clearly Tuchel has been impressed.

Speaking before his call-up, Hill said: 'It’s every kid’s dream, isn’t it? You grow up watching the Three Lions on TV, for the World Cup, the Euros. It’s one of the greatest honours you can have in football.'

Football is in the blood for Hill. His father, Matt, made more than 550 appearances in the Football League for the likes of Preston North End, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Sheffield United and Queens Park Rangers as a defender.

Hill played for England at age group level, pictured here kissing his now wife after a game

Hill's younger brother, Tyler, is also in the game, playing for Torquay United in National League South.

But Matt did not pressure his sons into the sport, with James previously telling the Times: 'He didn’t want me to feel as though it’s a job.

'He wanted me to feel like I’m wanting to be here because I love doing it. This is my passion. It brings me happiness. He wanted me to come to that conclusion, not for him to make that decision for me.'

Hill was a well-rounded sportsman and his secondary school did not even play football. Instead, he excelled as a fly-half for the rugby side and impressed as a javelin thrower.

He attributes his success as being aided by trying his hand at different disciplines and it is paying off in abundance having had to largely bide his time before earning a first-team spot under Andoni Iraola last term, with loans to Blackburn and Hearts helping him develop.

Hill's progress flew somewhat under the radar somewhat for many fans outside of Bournemouth and his career peak of an England call-up coincides with domestic bliss.

Having married Tara in the summer, they welcomed their daughter Edie two months later.

Hill, pictured, heading the ball away against Ipswich has become one of the best defenders in the Premier League

'Becoming a dad is one of the most special things I’ve ever experienced in my life,' he said. 'There isn’t a manual though, it’s just like, "Congratulations, you’ve got a baby". Then the door shuts! Hang on a minute. What am I supposed to do next? Is there a book for this? My wife has been absolutely incredible.'

He regularly shares pictures from both his professional and personal life on social media, putting wedding snaps alongside action shots of Bournemouth games.

Hill's England call-up will no doubt introduce him to a whole new audience previously unaware of the defender's capabilities, with only 34,000 Instagram followers at present.

The 24-year-old must now impress Tuchel enough to earn some game time when England play Croatia on Thursday in their next Nations League encounter.

#1813. Norway manager explains reason for ‘terribly tame’ Martin Odegaard performance

Arsenal skipper Martin Odegaard was accused of delivering a ‘terribly tame’ performance for Norway in their Nations League win over Wales.

The Gunners’ captian completed 90 minutes as Stale Solbakken’s side ran out comfortable 3-1 winners courtesy of goals from Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland.

Odegaard, however, appeared far from his usual energetic self and his lack of spark was noted by former Norway international Kjetil Rekdal.

‘I think he was terribly tame today,’ Rekdal told TV 2. ‘He looked tired and didn’t have the movement he usually has.

‘I think he was much less visible than he usually is.’

Solbakken, however, explained that his inspirational playmaker overcame an illness that caused Odegaard to endure a sleepless night prior to the match.

‘We have had a captain who has been lying around all night and spitting, and who was allowed to take some other liberties than he was supposed to,’ he said.

‘If you lie down all night and throw up, that’s it. All credit to him for going the distance. We had a conversation during the break that he should just drive from the start and let us know when the tank was empty.’

Odegaard’s commitment to the cause was praised by several of his teammates, including David Moller Wolfe.

#1812. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.
