#1749. Panama vs Curacao - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 13 Nov 2026 15:07

The first semi-finalist in this season’s CONCACAF Nations League will be decided on Sunday, when Panama host Curacao in the second leg of that tie at Estadio Rommel Fernandez in Panama City.

It is all to play for this weekend after these teams drew 0-0 at Ergilio Hato Stadium in Willemstad on Thursday evening.

It was another match full of missed opportunities for Panama on Thursday, who are now without a normal time win in eight successive internationals.

Over that stretch, they have netted a goal or fewer in each game but have not conceded more than one in their last four outings.

Thomas Christiansen’s men have won two of their last three internationals at Estadio Rommel Fernandez and have not lost a Nations League outing at that venue this decade.

This is the first time they go into the second leg of a Nations League quarter-final tie without an advantage, but the Panamanians have never lost at home in this phase of the competition.

Panama have also not lost to a Caribbean side since Jamaica beat them 1-0 in the 2024 Nations League third-place match.

Sunday will mark the second time they welcome Curacao to Panama, with Los Canaleros previously beating them on home soil, 2-1 in 2021.

At times it looked like they were holding on, but to their credit Curacao managed to pull out a result in the opening leg.

That extended their unbeaten run in the Nations League to 10 matches dating back to their promotional campaign in League B in 2024-25.

On Sunday, they can win their first-ever knockout match in this tournament and reach the semi-finals of a CONCACAF competition for the first time since capturing the 2017 Caribbean Cup.

Meanwhile, Dick Advocaat’s team can extend their unbeaten run versus CONCACAF opposition to 13 matches this weekend, with their last defeat against their own region occurring in the 2025 Gold Cup (a 2-1 loss to Honduras).

Curacao boast a 100% record in this competition when netting the opening goal, winning two of their three group matches in that scenario this season.

The Blue Wave have never lost a Nations League match on Central American soil, including a 4-3 comeback win at Costa Rica in this season’s group phase.

On the Panama side, Manuel Moran is still seeking his first caps after being an unused substitute on Thursday, while Cesar Blackman returned to the pitch, coming on for Jorge Gutierrez.

Orlando Mosquera was back between the sticks in the opening leg of this tie after Eddie Roberts got the call in their last friendly versus Ecuador.

At Curacao, we saw four new faces in their starting 11 this week who did not begin their match versus Trinidad and Tobago, including Armando Obispo, Joshua Brenet, Tahith Chong and Ar’jany Martha.

Eloy Room and Leandro Bacuna remain tied for first in all-time caps with the national team as the former collected his second clean sheet of the competition this season.

Mosquera; Murillo, Cordoba, Andrade, Gutierrez; Harvey, Griffith; Carrasquilla, Barcenas, Diaz; Vergara

Room; Sambo, Gaari, Obispo, Carolina; Comenencia, L. Bacuna; Brenet, Margaritha, Gorre; J. Bacuna

While we expect Panama to have the bulk of possession again, they seem to lack that decisive touch in the attacking third, and we believe an in-form Curacao side will hold their nerve in the big moments on Sunday.

A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1745. Jair Cunha eyes Brazil start after denying Erling Haaland in Forest win

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 15:17, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 15:17

Nottingham Forest defender Jair Cunha could be handed another Brazil start under Carlo Ancelotti just days after producing a remarkable performance against Erling Haaland and Manchester City in the Premier League.

The 21-year-old Brazilian has emerged as one of the most encouraging stories of Forest's difficult start to the season, establishing himself in Oliver Glasner's defence after struggling for opportunities during his first year in England.

His progress was underlined last Saturday when he scored the opening goal in Forest's 3-1 victory over Manchester City before producing a crucial goal-line clearance to deny Haaland.

Now, with Paris Saint-Germain captain Marquinhos absent through injury, Cunha is competing for a place alongside Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhaes in Ancelotti's starting XI for Brazil's friendly against Japan on Saturday.

The Nottingham Forest youngster faces competition from Manchester City defender Vitor Reis, but his recent performances have strengthened his case for another opportunity on the international stage.

Cunha's emergence has been particularly impressive considering how slowly his Premier League career began.

Forest signed the central defender from Botafogo in July 2025, handing him a five-year contract after he had impressed at the Club World Cup.

Previously developed by Santos, Cunha arrived in England with considerable promise, having also helped Brazil win the South American Under-20 Championship.

However, his first campaign at the City Ground proved challenging.

The Brazilian struggled to establish himself amid repeated managerial changes, making only three senior appearances by the end of February 2026.

He also spent time with Forest's Under-21 side while adapting to English football, before gradually receiving more opportunities during the closing months of the season.

The arrival of Glasner and another pre-season in England have helped accelerate his development.

Cunha has established himself as a regular option in Forest's three-man defence, alongside fellow Brazilian Murillo and experienced Serbian international Nikola Milenkovic.

His emergence is particularly noteworthy given the competition for places, with Forest having also invested approximately €40m (£35m) in the signing of Ousmane Diomande.

Although Glasner's side have struggled for consistency, Cunha has demonstrated the combination of physical presence, pace and composure in possession that initially attracted Forest to him.

Those attributes were evident in the victory over Manchester City on November 7.

After just six minutes, Cunha pressed high up the pitch, dispossessed Josko Gvardiol and drove into the penalty area before beating Gianluigi Donnarumma.

It was the defender's first goal for Forest and helped lay the foundations for a memorable victory, with Liam Delap subsequently scoring twice against his former club.

Yet Cunha's most important defensive contribution came shortly before half time.

Haaland had rounded goalkeeper Matz Sels and appeared set to score, only for the Brazilian to recover and clear the Norwegian's effort off the line.

The intervention preserved Forest's two-goal advantage and provided another illustration of the youngster's growing confidence at Premier League level.

Cunha's improvement has already earned recognition from Ancelotti, who included him in his Brazil squad for the September and October international fixtures.

The defender made his senior debut against Australia and collected three caps during that international period.

He started the second meeting with Australia, completing 69 accurate passes and recording 78 touches, while impressing with his ability to track opposing forwards and cover space behind the defensive line.

Those qualities could prove useful as Ancelotti continues assessing his options in central defence.

Marquinhos remains an established figure in the national team, but his absence from the current squad has created an opportunity for younger defenders to impress.

Gabriel Magalhaes is among the leading candidates to start against Japan, leaving Cunha and Vitor Reis competing to partner the Arsenal centre-back.

Cruzeiro defender Jonathan Jesus is another option in the squad, while Arthur Dias offers additional cover.

Cunha's familiarity with the demands of Premier League football could work in his favour, particularly after his performance against one of the competition's most dangerous forwards.

However, his inclusion in the squad preceded the Manchester City victory, meaning the display against Haaland should be viewed as further evidence of his progress rather than the reason for his international selection.

Ancelotti has also indicated that the November fixtures will bring the current period of experimentation to a close, increasing the importance of opportunities for players hoping to establish themselves in his longer-term plans.

Brazil face Japan at Singapore's National Stadium on Saturday before meeting the hosts on November 17.

Cunha is already being considered for a starting role, with Sports Mole's predicted Brazil lineup against Japan placing him alongside Gabriel in central defence.

Whether Ancelotti selects him or opts for Reis remains to be seen, but the contrast with his situation at Forest earlier this year is striking.

A defender who was struggling for regular first-team football just months ago is now pushing for a place in Brazil's starting XI, having delivered arguably his finest Premier League performance against Manchester City.

#1744. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1743. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton and Hove Albion Verbruggen; Wieffer, Vuskovic, Boscagli, Dunk; Gross, Ayari; Gomez, Hinshelwood, De Cuyper; Rutter

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Aston Villa Bizot; Cash, Torres, Lindelof, Maatsen; Barkley, Kamara; McGinn, Gomes, Hemmings; Buendia

Subs Suzuki, Mings, Ruggeri, Bogarde, Alysson, Rowe, Burrowes, Garnacho, Lynch

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Reis, Kovacic, Cherki, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush

Bournemouth Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Cook, Scott; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. #1741. I've worked for 20 years to try and play at a World Cup... I was never going to let heart procedure get in the way of my dream, says McTominay

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 17:37 EST, 10 November 2026

AS he lay on a hospital bed in Boston, just 48 hours or so before the start of the World Cup back in the summer, Scott McTominay could easily have felt like his dream was being snatched away from him.

Having played such a key role in helping Scotland get back to the Promised Land after 28 years in exile, McTominay was about to go under an anaesthetic for a heart procedure.

The issue became known at Scotland’s training base in Charlotte. By the time the team had flown to Boston for the opening match against Haiti, it was a matter of urgency.

McTominay was taken straight from the airport to the hospital via a police escort. Nobody would have blamed him if football had been the last thing on his mind.

Nor would anyone have blamed him if he pulled out of the squad altogether. But, after talking it through with the doctors, nothing was more certain in his own mind than that he would play.

McTominay played in all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup despite the procedure

Yet, nonetheless, a very obvious question remained. Was there ever any concern from his family? Was there ever a feeling that sitting it out would be the safest course of action?

‘No, I wouldn’t have listened to it [if they had said that],’ explained the Scotland midfielder. ‘All my family and friends had just flown 10 hours for the first game of the World Cup.

‘I didn’t sit there thinking I might not play. That would never be the case. I was always going to play in that game. Maybe selfishly, I don’t know but that’s football.

‘Players play with injuries all the time when they’re not quite right and it might be to the detriment of the team. I was fully functional.

‘It was in my hands. The medical team reassured me it was safe to play and they said: "What do you think?" I said: "Let’s go for it".'

McTominay essentially needed the rhythm and beat of his heart to be reset.

The midfielder struggles during the 1-0 defeat to Morocco at Boston Stadium

Explaining the procedure in more detail, he said: ‘Atrial fibrillation is a fairly normal routine thing for people in general.

‘They might not know that they have it. But when you’re an elite athlete in general across the board, across football, across sports in general, you know if you’ve got something that’s different.

‘Whenever you’re running and you check your pulse and it’s got a slight irregular beat there, it feels like your heart’s coming out of your chest.

‘Not obviously as bad as that but that’s the sensation that you have that it’s pumping, but not a regular heartbeat that’s like: “Bum, bum, bum, bum”.

‘Mine’s going: “Bum, bu-bu-bum, bum, bu-bu-bum”. So you know the difference.

‘We went to Boston, we got a police escort to go and get the shock then that was it to be honest. After that, I was back in normal rhythm, which is how a healthy heart should be then I went and played the game two days later.

‘The heat was tough, that was probably the hardest part. But I’ve worked for 20 years as a young footballer and as a professional to get to that point. To try and play well at a World Cup.

‘If things were a bit different in the second or third game, you never know what might have happened.’

McTominay has been in fine form for Napoli this season following a further procedure

McTominay played in all three matches against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil as Scotland were knocked out at the group stage.

Many fans had questioned his form, along with other senior players like John McGinn and Andy Robertson, albeit completely oblivious to what was going on behind the scenes.

Asked for his overall reflections on the World Cup, the Napoli midfielder said: ‘It wasn’t easy. Probably two, three weeks of putting my head in the sand, thinking we let one slip. That was just the bottom line.

‘It took me longer than what I normally would do to get over disappointment in football, to know the reason why I felt like it was just because we could have done more.

‘But in general it was probably one of the worst moments of my career.

‘Then I had the surgery at the start of the season. It went well and there was no doubt in my mind I would come back from it.

‘After the operation, I had three weeks at home. I didn’t watch as much football as I normally do. Normally I watch games relentlessly every night.

‘So I had three weeks of resting my mind more than anything to try and come back in a better state. I’m feeling good now and looking forward to getting going again.’

McTominay eventually underwent corrective surgery back at the start of the season which ruled him out of Scotland’s opening four fixtures in the Nations League.

Now back on form for Napoli and back in the Scotland squad, he’s desperate to make an impact for Sebastien Pocognoli’s new-look side.

Scotland will face North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday night before rounding off their Nations League campaign with a trip to Switzerland.

So often Scotland's talisman, he has returned ahead of the Nations League double header

McTominay spoke highly of the new head coach and has been impressed by his methods in training so far this week.

‘I like it, I like his ideas a lot,’ he said of Scotland’s new boss. ‘Whenever I first had a meeting with him, I liked the way that he wants to play the game.

‘High energy, high tempo, and obviously different ideas tactically on how to build up and the high-pressure situations we’ll find ourselves in, going against teams and trying to nick it off them and create goals that way, which is another tool in how to score goals and put the ball in the back of the opposition’s net.

‘So yeah, the early signs are really good, and he’s a great guy as well, as are his staff. I’m looking forward to it.

‘I feel like I’m a young kid that is coming back to learn as much as possible, and to try and soak it all in and help the younger ones realise the opportunity that they have in Scotland and in football in general.

‘They don’t maybe realise how far they can push themselves to break boundaries and limits in the game, and that can really pay off.’

#1740. Carlo Ancelotti reveals Brazil selection deadline for five youngsters

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 15:41

Carlo Ancelotti has confirmed that Brazil's period of experimentation will effectively come to an end after November's international break, placing greater significance on the opportunities available to five uncapped youngsters.

The five-time world champions are preparing to face Japan on Saturday before taking on Singapore next Tuesday, with Ancelotti using the final two fixtures of 2026 to assess players who could feature in his plans for the 2028 Copa America and 2030 World Cup.

Manchester City winger Allan, Cruzeiro defender Jonathan Jesus, Corinthians midfielder Andre Luiz and Shakhtar Donetsk pair Marlon Gomes and Alisson Santana are all hoping to make their senior international debuts.

Their inclusion follows Brazil's disappointing last-16 elimination against Norway at the 2026 World Cup, which prompted Ancelotti to accelerate the development of a new generation.

However, the Italian has now indicated that the time for widespread changes is running out, with a more settled squad expected when Brazil reconvene in March 2027.

Speaking at a press conference in Singapore on Friday, Ancelotti explained that he had gathered sufficient information from the international windows since the World Cup to begin narrowing his options.

"This period of experimentation will end during this international break. Next time, we will narrow down the squad a little more," Ancelotti told reporters, as quoted by ge.globo.

"It has been a period that has given us a lot of information about the young players. We know we have youngsters with a lot of talent who are very committed, and that gives us confidence for the future.

"We have players of a very high level. We have cover in some positions, a little less in others, but we have time."

The former Real Madrid manager also suggested that the core of his future squad was already taking shape, although he left the door open for players currently outside the national team.

"There are some players we have looked at who are not here and could be involved next time, but there aren't many. The squad is more or less settled," he added.

Brazil's rebuilding process began in September, when Ancelotti selected eight first-time call-ups for matches against Australia and India.

The Selecao subsequently recorded two victories and a draw, with several emerging players receiving their first opportunities at senior international level.

The forthcoming encounters against Japan and Singapore therefore represent another opportunity for Ancelotti to evaluate his options before moving towards greater continuity in selection.

Among the latest additions, Marlon Gomes could have one of the clearest opportunities to influence Ancelotti's plans, with the Shakhtar midfielder being assessed in a deeper role during preparations for the Japan fixture.

The 22-year-old, formerly of Vasco da Gama, has developed into a versatile central midfielder capable of contributing defensively and carrying possession into advanced areas.

According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, Gomes has averaged 4.5 tackles and completed 96% of his passes across four Champions League appearances this season.

His versatility could be particularly useful as Ancelotti considers different midfield combinations involving Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes, Manchester United's Andrey Santos and Aston Villa's Joao Gomes.

Another intriguing inclusion is Manchester City youngster Allan, who received his first Brazil call-up despite playing just 10 minutes of Premier League football following his summer arrival from Palmeiras.

The 22-year-old has struggled for regular opportunities under Enzo Maresca, although his defensive commitment and ability to operate on either flank offer Ancelotti a different option in attack.

Allan recorded four goals and three assists in 21 Brazilian top-flight appearances for Palmeiras, according to the statistics highlighted by Trivela.

Jonathan Jesus, meanwhile, provides another possibility at centre-back, having established himself at Cruzeiro this season.

The 22-year-old is naturally right-footed but regularly operates on the left side of central defence, where Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhaes is among Ancelotti's established options.

Ancelotti previously praised Jonathan's physical strength, pace and intelligence, while his distribution could also prove valuable in Brazil's attempts to build from the back.

Corinthians midfielder Andre Luiz, 20, offers energy and the ability to arrive in attacking positions from deep, having contributed four goals and two assists in 24 league appearances.

Shakhtar winger Alisson Santana, 21, has also caught the eye with his direct running and one-on-one ability, averaging 4.3 successful dribbles per match in the Ukrainian league this season.

Whether all five newcomers receive playing time remains uncertain, particularly against a Japan side that will provide Brazil with a demanding test on Saturday.

Ancelotti has already indicated that he wants to experiment with Bournemouth forward Rayan in midfield, while Marlon Gomes has been considered for a defensive midfield role.

Those decisions could offer an early indication of which younger players are closest to earning a regular place when Brazil begin preparing more directly for the 2028 Copa America.

#1739. Harry Kane receives new England GOAT verdict as 120-goal prediction made (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 13 Nov 2026 16:30

Harry Kane has usurped Wayne Rooney as the best England player of his generation, but he still trails the 1966 World Cup winners among the all-time greats, Darren Bent has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Kane now stands alone in both appearances and goals for the England men's national team, having broken Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps with his 126th senior international outing against Croatia on Thursday night.

The Bayern Munich talisman had already held the England all-time goals record for over three years, surpassing Wayne Rooney's 53 in March 2023, and his penalty in the Nations League took him onto 92 for the men's team.

Kane also reached the zenith of individual footballing achievements by winning the Ballon d'Or last month, but the England captain is yet to lead his nation to a World Cup or Euros triumph.

As a result, ex-England, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur striker Bent - who scored four goals in 13 England games - believes that Kane is still not quite in the conversation with Sir Bobby Moore and Sir Bobby Charlton.

"It's really difficult to go against those boys from the 60s. They climbed the mountain and won the World Cup, and there will obviously have been Ballon d'Or winners in that team as well," Bent told Sports Mole via MrQ sportsbook.

"It's difficult to automatically put Harry Kane above them. But certainly in my generation, it would either be him or Wayne Rooney as the greatest England player.

"When you look at Kane being the all-time record caps holder and the all-time record goalscorer, it's hard to put Rooney above him. I'd probably say that, for this modern generation, it would be Kane.

"If Kane were to win the World Cup, he would automatically go into a bracket alongside the likes of Bobby Charlton as one of England's greatest players. But he's already in the conversation, and that's massive in itself. To put him in the conversation with those greats, legends and icons is special."

With an unrivalled 92 goals in an unparalleled 126 caps, Kane finds the net at a rate of 0.73 goals per game for the England national team, compared to Rooney's 0.44 and Charlton's 0.46.

The Tottenham legend turns 34 next year, but barring injury or an unexpected early retirement, Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup are very much on the horizon.

Asking AI to predict how many England goals Kane could rack up before retirement, the 33-year-old is projected to find the net 120 times for his country, should he call it quits after the 2030 World Cup.

Such a total would currently put Kane third on the all-time international scorers list, above Ali Daei (108) and only behind Lionel Messi (126) and Cristiano Ronaldo (146).

Kane is already joint-sixth in the charts alongside Robert Lewandowski, and two more will take him level with Romelu Lukaku's 94 for Belgium, while he needs three to match Sunil Chhetri's 95 for India.

Darren Bent was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of MrQ Live Casino.

#1738. New Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino breaks down in tears as he makes "very sad" admission

By Ben Sully | 13 Nov 2026 16:45, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 20:26

Mauricio Pochettino has admitted he has made "one of the most difficult decisions" of his career by leaving his role with the USMNT to become Manchester United's head coach.

Pochettino, who took the USA job in 2024, led the country to the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup before signing a new contract through to 2030.

However, Pochettino will not see out that deal after Man United activated the £7.4m release clause in his contract to appoint him as Michael Carrick's successor.

The 54-year-old broke down in tears during his first press conference since being confirmed as the new Red Devils boss, admitting the process of the appointment happened "so quickly".

"In some part, this is a very sad decision," Pochettino said in Friday's press conference.

"In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true.

"It all happened so quickly. By Sunday afternoon, there was contact. You always were transparent and always tried to build something together.

"We learned a lot from you all, this amazing country and you amazing people. This is one of the most difficult decisions of my career. Thank you so much."

Pochettino admitted the chance to manage a club of Man United's stature was too good to turn down when asked why he opted to leave his post despite only recently signing a four-year contract.

"It's obvious," Pochettino added. They [U.S. Soccer] know that not many opportunities can happen in your career like a side the size of Manchester United.

"When that arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

The Argentine was speaking ahead of the USA's CONCACAF Nations League clash against Haiti on Saturday.

Pochettino will oversee the two-legged tie before travelling to Manchester to officially take over the reins at Old Trafford ahead of a Premier League encounter against Liverpool on November 22.

The Red Devils are currently languishing in the Premier League drop zone after winning just one of their 10 top-flight outings this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It wasn’t an immediate fit, though, and he was called overexcited, thanks to his yellow card record. Yet, he’s settled and now is a key figure in a three-man defence and picking out his best traits are difficult because there are so many.

#1736. Mauricio Pochettino's record against every Premier League club after Man United appointment

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 13 Nov 2026 17:28

Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, with the Argentine replacing Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after the club’s worst-ever start to a Premier League season left them in the relegation zone.

The 54-year-old, who led the United States to the 2026 World Cup, where they topped Group D before a 4-1 last-16 defeat to Belgium, has now signed for the Red Devils on a deal that runs until the summer of 2029.

With Old Trafford the seventh senior post of a managerial career that began at Espanyol in January 2009, Pochettino returns to club football for the first time since leaving Chelsea by mutual consent in May 2024.

Having also managed Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford with a wealth of Premier League experience ahead of his first game in charge, a daunting trip to Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

With that in mind, Sports Mole takes a look at Pochettino’s record against every club in the current Premier League, as well as the sides he is yet to come up against.

Pochettino’s Premier League record against Arsenal reads three wins, eight draws and four defeats from 15 games, a middling return given how rarely north London derbies are kind to anyone.

All three of those top-flight victories came with Spurs, while his last top-flight meeting with the Gunners ended in a 5-0 thrashing as Chelsea boss in April 2024.

Pochettino has a solid Premier League record against Aston Villa, winning four, drawing two and losing three of his nine meetings with them in the competition.

Three of those top-flight triumphs came with Tottenham, including a 3-1 victory on the opening weekend of 2019-20, but he failed to beat Villa in two Premier League attempts with Chelsea.

Bournemouth have been among Pochettino’s favourite Premier League opponents, with seven wins, two draws and just one defeat in 10 top-flight meetings.

The Argentine’s sides have so far scored 24 Premier League goals against the Cherries and conceded only four, including a 5-1 away win in 2015 and a 5-0 Boxing Day rout in 2018.

Brentford are the only current Premier League side Pochettino has faced in the competition and never beaten.

Both Premier League meetings came during his season at Chelsea, with the Bees winning 2-0 in October 2023 before the sides drew 2-2 in March 2024.

Pochettino boasts an impressive Premier League record against Brighton, winning five of his seven top-flight meetings with the Seagulls, including both with Chelsea.

The 54-year-old’s only Premier League defeat to Brighton came in a 3-0 loss in October 2019, just weeks before his Tottenham exit.

Pochettino faced Chelsea 13 times in the Premier League before managing them, winning five, drawing two and losing six.

The standout league result was Tottenham’s 5-3 victory on New Year’s Day 2015, while the infamous 2-2 Premier League draw at Stamford Bridge in May 2016 ended Spurs’ title hopes.

No club in this season’s Premier League has lost to Pochettino more often in the competition than Crystal Palace, who have managed one draw and one win in 15 top-flight meetings with him.

The Argentine’s sides have beaten Palace in 11 successive top-flight games, and his 2.67 Premier League points per game against them is his best against any club he has faced more than six times in the competition.

Everton have been kind Premier League opponents for Pochettino, who has won eight, drawn six and lost just two of his 16 top-flight meetings with them.

Pochettino’s teams have scored 33 Premier League goals against the Toffees, including a 6-2 win at Goodison Park in December 2018 and a 6-0 home thrashing with Chelsea in April 2024.

Pochettino has a perfect Premier League record against Fulham, winning all six top-flight meetings across his spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

The Argentine’s teams have scored 13 Premier League goals against the Cottagers and conceded just two, with Fulham yet to take a single top-flight point off him.

Hull City have had no answer to Pochettino either, losing all six of their Premier League meetings with him.

Pochettino’s teams have scored 19 top-flight goals and conceded three against the Tigers, highlighted by a 7-1 win at the KCOM Stadium on the final day of the 2016-17 Premier League season.

Pochettino has never faced Leeds United in the Premier League, with his only meeting with them coming in the FA Cup fifth round in February 2024.

Conor Gallagher’s 90th-minute winner gave his Chelsea side a 3-2 FA Cup win at Stamford Bridge, meaning Pochettino is yet to lose to the Whites in any competition.

Liverpool have been Pochettino’s toughest Premier League opponents, with just three wins, five draws and eight defeats in 16 top-flight meetings.

Pochettino’s 0.88 Premier League points per game against them is his worst against any club he has faced more than twice in the competition, and outside the league he also lost the 2019 Champions League final and the 2024 League Cup showpiece to the Reds.

Pochettino has won four, drawn five and lost seven of his 16 Premier League games against Manchester City.

Tottenham beat City in three successive top-flight meetings between September 2015 and October 2016, while his Chelsea side twice held Pep Guardiola’s side in the league, including a 4-4 thriller in November 2023.

Pochettino’s new employers have had the better of him in the Premier League, with five wins, three draws and seven defeats in 15 top-flight meetings.

The 54-year-old’s best league results against the Red Devils include a 3-0 win at Old Trafford in August 2018 and a 4-3 Chelsea victory in April 2024, though United also beat his Spurs side in the 2018 FA Cup semi-final.

Pochettino’s Premier League record against Newcastle is otherwise evenly balanced, with seven wins, one draw and six defeats in 14 games, and 23 goals both scored and conceded.

The Argentine’s Southampton side won 4-0 in a league clash in March 2014, but Tottenham crashed to a 5-1 loss at St James’ Park on the final day of the 2015-16 Premier League season.

Pochettino has faced Nottingham Forest twice in the Premier League, both times as Chelsea boss, winning one and losing one.

Anthony Elanga’s goal earned the Tricky Trees a 1-0 league win at Stamford Bridge in September 2023, before the Blues won 3-2 at the City Ground in the Premier League in May 2024.

Sunderland are one of three current Premier League clubs Pochettino is unbeaten against in the competition, with four wins and five draws in nine top-flight meetings.

The pick of those Premier League results was a 4-1 home win with Spurs in January 2016, although he has lost twice to the Black Cats in cup competitions.

Pochettino lost all three of his Premier League meetings with Tottenham as Southampton boss, two of them by 3-2 scorelines.

The Argentine manager then won both English top-flight  games against his old club with Chelsea in 2023-24, including a 4-1 victory in north London in November 2023.

Coventry City and Ipswich Town are the only current Premier League clubs Pochettino has never faced in any competition.

The Sky Blues ended a 25-year absence from the top flight this season, which means they were outside the Premier League throughout his spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

The Argentine’s first meeting with Coventry should come when they visit Old Trafford on Saturday, December 5, in what is scheduled to be his fourth league game in charge.

Ipswich’s only recent top-flight season came after he had left English football, and with United having already hosted them on August 30, his first meeting with the Tractor Boys is set for Portman Road on Saturday, April 17, 2027.
